newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle active at $66.00 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle active at $66.00 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold Thursday at $66.00 per cwt in brisk trading, up $1.00 from Wednesday and up $2.00 from the bulk of last week's sales, feedlot sources said.

About 26,200 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma, bringing the week to date figure to 109,200 including 22,800 formulated and 700 previously contracted cattle to be shipped this week, USDA said.
About 30,000 head sold in Kansas, bringing the weekly volume to 102,300, including 19,400 or about 19 percent previously contracted or formulated cattle, USDA said.
Strong beef demand spurred active packer buying in the past two weeks, with showlists for both weeks depleted, the feedlot sources said.
This week's Panhandle showlist was pegged at 77,500 head and the Kansas showlist was estimated at 75,300, they said.
Beef prices at Thursday's close were quoted up $0.71 to $0.87 per cwt, with choice heavyweight beef quoted up $0.87 at $97.38, USDA said. There were 256 fabricated loads sold.
The heavier-weight choice beef value was up $1.94 from the same period a week ago, according to USDA statistics.
